actions.justification: Mandatory first action - assess vital signs to establish baseline and identify any abnormalities guiding further workup.
Essential to identify the primary clinical concern and guide appropriate diagnostic and treatment pathway.
Assess overall patient condition including level of consciousness, appearance, and general well-being to complete initial evaluation.
Mental status assessment is a key component of the initial clinical evaluation to identify any neurological involvement or altered consciousness that may guide diagnosis and management.
Cardiovascular assessment is essential to evaluate perfusion, identify any hemodynamic instability, and rule out cardiac causes of the presentation.
Identifying a potential infection source is critical during initial assessment to guide appropriate diagnostic workup and treatment decisions.
Neurological assessment not yet completed - important to evaluate for any neurological deficits given unknown diagnosis at this stage
Abdominal assessment not yet completed - important to identify potential abdominal sources of pathology
Hydration status assessment helps guide fluid management decisions and identifies dehydration or fluid overload

Perform a comprehensive patient assessment to capture any remaining clinical details not covered by prior focused assessments, ensuring complete initial evaluation before moving to diagnostics or treatment.
Assess pain level as it has not yet been documented and is important for characterizing the patient's condition and guiding further workup.
Evaluate for signs of organ dysfunction to help identify the clinical syndrome and severity, which is critical before ordering targeted diagnostics or initiating treatment.
Complete systematic assessment by evaluating respiratory status - important to assess lung sounds, work of breathing, and oxygenation details even with SpO2 98%.
Assess skin for rashes, lesions, signs of infection, jaundice, or other findings that may inform the working diagnosis.
Assess musculoskeletal status to complete the full physical examination and identify any joint swelling, tenderness, or other relevant findings.
Neurological assessment using NIHSS to quantify any neurological deficits and guide further workup, as the patient has had a comprehensive initial assessment but NIHSS has not yet been performed.
Baseline eGFR is important to assess renal function before any contrast imaging or nephrotoxic medications are considered.
Urine output assessment helps evaluate end-organ perfusion and fluid status, complementing the hydration and organ dysfunction assessments already completed.
Establishing IV access is a foundational step for any patient requiring further diagnostics or treatment, enabling blood draws and medication administration.
Given the comprehensive assessment already completed, specialist input will help guide targeted diagnostic workup and management plan based on the clinical findings.
If infection source has been identified during assessment, empiric antibiotic therapy may be indicated pending further diagnostic confirmation.
Given the completed neurological assessment including NIHSS and cardiovascular workup, aspirin is indicated if ischemic stroke or TIA is suspected and no contraindications are present.
Patient requires inpatient monitoring and further workup based on completed assessments. Admission is appropriate pending diagnostic confirmation.
